Head Teacher's Welcome – School Values & Ethos
A warm welcome to the Rhyl Community Primary School website. We are an inclusive and vibrant primary school in the heart of Camden where children thrive and excel.
News and Events
We are a very busy and exciting school and we have lots going on each week. We hope you enjoy finding out all about what is going on at Rhyl.
Calendar
SEND & Inclusion
We are incredibly proud of our provision for Inclusion & SEND at our school. You can find out more here about how we support children and families to provide an excellent provision at Rhyl.
Outdoor Classroom
We bring the curriculum to life for our children through outdoor learning, sustainability and Forest Schools. Rhyl is proud to be a Green Flag school.
Rhyl Kitchen Classroom
Rhyl Kitchen Classroom is where pupils enjoy our unique plot-to-plate curriculum. It is also available to hire for children's parties and other events. Find out more about our amazing community kitchen.

Our children are the most important people at our school and are fully involved in decision making at our school. Opportunities for Pupil Voice are many and varied at Rhyl.

pageCache.pageTitle: Message from the Executive Head - Rhyl Community Primary School
pageCache.text:
Message from the Executive Head
Executive Head Teacher’s Welcome
Welcome to Rhyl Community Primary School. We are very proud of our school and we hope our website gives you a real sense of what makes Rhyl such a special place to learn, grow and thrive.
Rhyl is a vibrant, happy and inclusive community school in the heart of Camden, welcoming children and families from a wide diversity of backgrounds. We offer high-quality educational provision from the very start of a child’s learning journey — from our 2-year-old provision through to Nursery and beyond — ensuring the best possible foundations for every child.
Our curriculum is broad, rich and creative, with a strong emphasis on the arts and wider learning opportunities that inspire curiosity and imagination. Children benefit from working with artists, specialists and professionals across a range of disciplines, as well as through educational visits and real-world experiences that bring learning to life. We value and nurture every child’s unique talents, helping them to grow as confident, motivated and independent learners.
We are fortunate to have exceptional facilities and learning spaces across our school, designed to support high-quality teaching and learning. One of our sites has recently undergone extensive renovations, providing modern, flexible and inspiring environments that promote creativity, collaboration and curiosity. Our classrooms and shared spaces reflect our commitment to providing the very best learning experience for every child.
We are ambitious for our children and committed to achieving the highest standards, both academically and personally. Our staff are dedicated, experienced and passionate about ensuring that every child is supported to succeed and to flourish.
As a community school, we are proud to be at the heart of local life. Our school buildings host a wide range of services and activities for the wider community — from baby groups and early years sessions to adult learning and community events — helping us build strong partnerships and lifelong connections with our families.
Rhyl is a place where children feel safe, respected and celebrated for who they are. We foster an ethos of inclusion, respect and high aspiration, and we work closely with parents, carers and our wider community to ensure every child has the opportunity to thrive.
You can read more about our school values and ethos by clicking on the image below.
Visitors are warmly welcome and we would very much like to show you around our school so that you can see for yourself some of the work we are doing first hand.
Executive Head Teacher

Rhyl Kitchen Classroom
Rhyl Kitchen Classroom is our new venue for top quality food education. This fully-equipped community kitchen is located in the heart of our food garden, allowing us to integrate our teaching and learning from ‘plot to plate’.
Find out more on the project website – including how to hire the building and garden for children’s parties and other events. And follow us on social media @rhylkitchen.
It was a huge team effort to build Rhyl Kitchen Classroom, involving five years of fundraising in which we raised £200,000 from scratch. Back in 2016 a group of school staff cycled from the school to the Eiffel Tower in Paris in the first phase of this epic mission.
This building enables us to take our teaching and learning to a new level. We have designed a new scheme of work that links to our Connected Curriculum and pupils will enjoy around six days of learning per academic year in this environment.
The project manager is teacher Tom Moggach, who leads on outdoor learning and food education at the school and founded the Rhyl Kitchen Classroom.

Outdoor Learning
At Rhyl, we are passionate about the power and importance of outdoor learning. Class teachers often take their learning outside as part of their creative curriculum.
Our specialist outdoor learning teacher also runs weekly sessions in our award-winning Outdoor Classroom – a garden and food plot where children learn about the natural environment, explore new flavours and follow the process of growing food from plot to plate. We also keep bees at the local city farm and have run Forest School sessions for a select cohort of children
With the help of the children, we built a wood-fired oven on site for outdoor cookery sessions. The garden is also the location of our amazing new Rhyl Kitchen Classroom, our community teaching kitchen.
In their regular sessions in the Outdoor Classroom, pupils follow a unique plot-to-plate curriculum which was first developed here at Rhyl then rolled out nationwide by the Jamie Oliver Food Foundation.
Rhyl has won a gold medal in both the good growing and curriculum awards in Camden In Bloom. We are an RHS Level 5 School and twice winners of the Greenest School in Camden Award.
You can keep up to date with the school’s outdoor learning and learn more about the Rhyl Kitchen Project using the images below.

SEND & Inclusion
At Rhyl Community Primary School, we are committed in ensuring that every child achieves the best possible outcomes regardless of their ethnicity, gender, cultural background, disability or learning need. We recognise our responsibilities under the Equality Act 2010 which came into force on 1st October 2010 and replaced existing equality legislation including the Disability Discrimination Act (DDA). In addition, at Rhyl we ensure we comply with our duties in the Special Education Needs Disability Regulations 2014. For further information on how we make the curriculum accessible for all, please read our SEND Policy and Accessibility Plan.
Our practices and procedures are embedded into school life to ensure pupils’ special educational needs are identified swiftly. We consider each of the pupils when planning and provide a curriculum which is accessible to all, whatever their individual needs. We acknowledge that some pupils require additional support to ensure access to a full curriculum and, where appropriate, a range of support strategies, including personalised curriculums, are implemented. You can learn more by clicking on the icons below.
If additional specialist advice and support is necessary, we seek external agency support such as speech and language therapists, school nurse and educational psychologists. We are committed to effective collaboration between all agencies working with a child and a multi-disciplinary approach to meeting pupils’ special educational needs. All staff at Rhyl are provided with training, coaching and support to develop and refine good practice when working with SEND pupils.
If you wish to talk to us about your child’s needs or the provision in place, please speak to your child’s class teacher or any member of our Inclusion Team, which is led by our Executive Head Teacher, Don McGibbon, working alongside our SENDCo, Amirthi Perera. Our SENDCo, SEND Teacher, Children and Family Support Worker, Zara Lee, and Learning Mentors, Denise Folwell and Jenny Sampson can all be contacted by email at admin@rhylprim.camden.sch.uk.
